source_note: `source` fields name the file owning the field's authoritative default. Line numbers are intentionally omitted — they drift on every reformat and the file/symbol name is the stable contract.
range_policy: advisory — `min`/`max` fields are UI hints documenting the values authors have validated; the parser/validator enforces only positivity (numeric fields) and enum membership (enum fields). Out-of-range-but-positive values are accepted at parse time.

entries.description: step2 backend. 'cpu' is the numba master kernel, the numerical reference. 'gpu' is the P-layout / bit-packed CuPy backend (Step2SparseSession): BOLD stays bit-packed on device, EM state is carried on the P = nnz(boundary_mask) support instead of the dense (N, L) grid, and the outer-EM closure leaves (L16/L17/L18) run on-device too.
entries.notes: 'gpu' contract: docs/step2_sparse_design.md; ~130x faster than 'cpu' at S=10 (4.1 s vs 538 s) and run-to-run deterministic. It requires a seed mesh with ceil(D/8) <= 256, i.e. seed_mesh 'fsaverage3' in bold_inputs.json, num_clusters <= 512 (init_hard_labels' per-lane accumulator ceiling) and n_grad_components <= 11772 (connect_u's shared memory); larger configurations run on 'cpu'. Its VRAM is bounded by the per-subject gradient and the (S, T, L, D) fp32 s_t_nu / X_dot_sl pair plus the packed BOLD cache (which streams when it does not fit), not by a dense (S, N, L) s_lambda. Params_Final.mat is unchanged on every backend: dense fp64 theta, compressed. The dense CuPy port that held 'gpu' until 2026-09 (fp32 flush-to-zero E-step, nondeterministic) was removed; 'gpu_sparse', the name this backend shipped under beside it, is rejected.

entries.notes: auto picks eager_bitpacked when the (S, T, N, ⌈D/8⌉) uint8 packed cache (1 bit/cell, ~72 MB per subject at T=6/fsa6) plus the resident device state fits in free device memory minus gpu_cache_safety_margin_gb, else stream (Step2SparseSession._resolve_cache_mode; 'stream' costs 2 host->device visits per subject per EM iteration). On backend_step2='cpu' the same knob picks the loader's host-side bit-packed cache ('auto' / 'eager_bitpacked') or per-call disk decode ('stream'). The legacy unpacked-uint8 'eager' mode was removed 2026-06.
